name: file.stat
description: Returns metadata for a file or directory: type, size, timestamps, and Win32 attributes. Tolerates both files and directories.

path.description: Absolute path to a file or directory.

type.description: `file` for regular files; `directory` for directories; `link` for reparse points / symlinks / junctions; `other` for anything else (devices, pipes, sockets).

size.description: Byte size. Zero for directories. Symlink size is the target's size when resolved.

mtime_unix.description: Modification time as Unix epoch seconds. Last write to the content.

ctime_unix.description: Creation time as Unix epoch seconds. NT-era FAT filesystems may report 0 (no creation timestamp tracking).

atime_unix.description: Access time as Unix epoch seconds. May be 0 if access-time tracking is disabled (FAT12/16, or NTFS with disablelastaccess set).

flags.description: Win32 FILE_ATTRIBUTE_* flags currently set. Per issue #93 — zero-cost set sourced from GetFileAttributesEx output. Cloud-file flags (recall_on_*) are Windows 10+; older Windows omits them.

x-implementations.name: get_file_attributes_ex
x-implementations.description: Win32 `GetFileAttributesExW(GetFileExInfoStandard)` — single call yielding size, three timestamps, and attribute flags. NT 5+.

x-implementations.name: find_first_file
x-implementations.description: Win32 `FindFirstFileA` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where GetFileAttributesEx is unavailable. Same WIN32_FIND_DATA shape (size, timestamps, attributes).

windows-modern.description: GetFileAttributesExW. Reparse-point detection via FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT in attributes; resolved type is `link`. Long paths via `\\?\` prefix automatic when input exceeds MAX_PATH.

windows-classic.description: GetFileAttributesExW on NT 5+; FindFirstFile on NT 4 / 9x. Reparse points are NT 5+ — classic on NT 4 / 9x reports `file` or `directory` only. FAT12/FAT16 mtime resolution is 2 seconds (DOS file time); ctime may be 0.
